title: Pre-Market — Friday, Nov 6, 2026
html:
Chips bounce, the Dow slips, and the jobs report decides the open.

Good morning, the desk. Yesterday's crash left SPY sitting on a Fibonacci shelf. Overnight the beaten-up chip stocks bounced hard while the safer names slipped. Here's what changed since last night's debrief.

The one thing

SPY is $734.90 pre-market, just above yesterday's $733 close and the $732.44 shelf. The 8:30 jobs report will move it before the bell, so treat any price before 8:30 as a placeholder.

The level that matters hasn't changed: the $722–727 floor, where the 200-day average sits. Above it, the uptrend is bruised but alive. On the upside, SPY needs to get back over $744 and stay there before buyers are in charge again. A small bounce in between, like this one, changes nothing.

Overnight in plain words

  • Futures: S&P 500 futures are up about 0.2–0.3%. Nasdaq 100 futures are up about 1.4% as chips bounce. Dow futures are down about 0.8–1.1%. Yesterday's split has flipped. Pre-market: SPY +0.3%, QQQ +1.5%, IWM +0.2%.
  • Asia · Europe: Asia caught yesterday's AI selloff: Japan's Nikkei fell about 6%, which puts it in a bear market (20% or more below its high). Korea's Kospi fell more than 6% and hit a circuit breaker, a forced trading pause. Hong Kong and Shanghai fell about 1%. Europe is trading lower after Wall Street's drop.
  • Oil · rates · VIX: Oil is a bit lower on hopes for a US–Iran deal: WTI about $89.80 (−0.8%), Brent about $97.60 (−0.7%). The 10-year yield is about 4.84%, down a little. The VIX, the market's fear gauge, is about 26.8, down 5% from yesterday's 28 but still high.
  • Headline: The fear is still about AI: investors worry the Democrats' midterm wins will slow data-center building. Yesterday's selloff erased about $2.3 trillion in market value, and retail traders were heavy sellers. Airbnb's beat-and-raise last night is the good news.

SPY at the open

Pre-market: $734.90

  • $781.62 — Oct 6 record high
  • $765–766 — Ceiling · 20- and 50-day
  • $750–752 — Old floor, now ceiling
  • $743–745 — First test up · 3 Fibs
  • $732.44 — Yesterday's close area · 1.382
  • $722–727 — The line · 200-day + 1.618 + 38.2%
  • $713 — Next stop · 2.0 extension
  • $701–704 — Deep floor · 50% + 2.382
  • If SPY opens above $745… it has cleared the first test and three Fib levels at once. Don't buy the first minute. If it holds above $744 through the first 30 minutes, the SPY call setup from last night is live, with $751 next.
  • If it holds between $727 and $745… this is the most likely case. It's a bounce inside a damaged market. No SPY trade. Watch whether the bounce fades back toward $733 by mid-morning.
  • If it opens below $727… it is already testing the line. A close below $722 means the selling has spread beyond AI. Then we sit in cash and stop looking for calls.

Movers on the Watchlist

  • ABNB $189.00 (+11.1%) — Beat, raised. Airbnb beat last night: $3.16 a share on $4.87 billion in revenue, and it raised its full-year outlook. It's trading near its 52-week high of $193. Plan: Good news for your travel ideas (HLT, RCL, DAL). ABNB itself is a gap you'd be chasing, so no trade.
  • HLT $366.74 (−0.8%) — Closer. Only 61 shares have traded, so the price means little. It sits just above yesterday's $365.87 low, which held. Plan: Closer to triggering. The entry is after the first 30 minutes, if it holds above $365.87 and gets back over $370. Airbnb's beat should help.
  • Chips: MU · AMD · DELL · BE $711.55 · $434.42 · $342.85 · $186.39 (+8.4% · +7.4% · +8.2% · +11.3%) — Bounce, not a turn. A bounce after 15–17% drops yesterday. NVDA is +3.7% ($188.33), SMH +5.1%, DRAM +8.9%, SMCI +5.6%. Asia's chip names kept falling overnight, so this is US traders buying the dip. Plan: No change to the downside idea, but don't short into a bounce. Last night's plan: NVDA puts only on a bounce that fails under $194–195. At $188, it's getting closer to that zone.
  • PLTR $158.86 (+2.5%) — Closer. Bouncing off its 200-day ($153.56) with the AI group. Plan: Closer to the $160 trigger. It still needs a green daily close above $160, not a pre-market print.
  • KO · AAPL $93.91 · $339.81 (−1.9% · −1.3%) — Rotation. No company news. Money is rotating out of yesterday's safe names into the beaten-up chips. AAPL is below its $343.10 20-day. Plan: No plays on either. It does explain why Dow futures are down.
  • SPCX $128.88 (+4.3%) — Bounce. Bouncing with the growth names after yesterday's 9% drop. Plan: No change.

No change on NOW ($101.69, a hair under its $101.80 swing low; still weak, so your downside idea holds but nothing to do yet), BA ($171.66, flat; still waiting for a failed rally), RCL ($321.20) and DAL ($85.21), both near yesterday's close.

Today's calendar

  • 8:30 a.m. October jobs report. Forecast +65,000 jobs (September was +29,000), unemployment 4.2%, wages +0.3% for the month. Strong wages raise the odds of a December Fed hike, which would hurt stocks. A weak number could help.
  • 9:10 a.m. St. Louis Fed's Musalem speaks about Fed independence. Watch for any comment on December.
  • 10:00 a.m. University of Michigan sentiment (forecast 48) and inflation expectations (1-year was 4.7%).
  • 12:15 p.m. Fed Vice Chair Bowman on bank rules. Also Bank of Japan's Ueda at 11:00 a.m. after Japan's 6% drop.
  • Earnings Moderna, Humana, Enbridge, Brookfield Asset Management and Charter before the open. None on your list, and none report tonight. Next: NVDA Nov 17, DELL Nov 24. No IV-crush risk (the drop in option prices after a report) this weekend.

Plays check (Options Playbook)

  • SPY Dec 18 $765 call — Wait. Not triggered. The entry needs SPY to test $722–727 and hold, or close back above $744. At $734.90 it's in between. Last night's price was about $622.
  • HLT Dec 18 $390 call — Closer to triggering. Pre-market is right on yesterday's $365.87 low, and Airbnb's beat helps travel. Enter only after the first 30 minutes, if it holds above $365.87 and trades back over $370. Use a limit order near the middle, because the spread was wide ($4.80 / $6.70). Exit on a close below $359.41.
  • DAL Dec 18 $85 call — Wait. No change. It needs a close back above $88; it's at $85.21. Cheaper oil is a small help. Exit on a close below $83.
  • No new plays. The chip bounce is big but it's a bounce after a crash, right before a jobs report. Puts on a bounce only work once it fails at a level, and NVDA's is $194–195.

Opening rule of the day

On a jobs-report morning after a crash, the first move is often the wrong one. Let the first 30 minutes settle before you act.

The 8:30 number will whip futures, and the open will whip again. With the VIX near 27, option spreads will be wide, so use limit orders only. Don't buy the chip bounce at the open; a +8% gap after a −17% day often fades. Let the 9:30–10:00 candle close, then check your levels: SPY $733 and $744, HLT $365.87 and $370.

Sources: Webull pre-market and overnight snapshots, watchlist and macro calendar (7:19 a.m. ET); Yahoo Finance live markets blog; TipRanks; TheStreet; last night's Debrief Nov 5.

Educational, not personal investment advice. Options can lose 100% of their value. Claude never places trades.
